primitives.name: Partial Membership Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: 2008, adapted for counts): each player i has a membership vector πi on the K-simplex (πi ~ Dirichlet(δ)); conditional on πi, each count variable j follows Poisson with rate = Πk λkj^{πik} (multiplicative compounding of cluster profiles by membership weights); λkj ~ Gamma priors.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'πi': "player i's membership vector on K-simplex (dimensionless)", 'δ': 'Dirichlet concentration parameter (dimensionless)', 'λkj': 'rate parameter for feature j in profile k (counts per minute)', 'xij': 'observed count for player i, feature j (counts)'}
primitives.assumptions: Players have soft role memberships; Poisson likelihoods; no overdispersion; static membership over season.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When K exceeds data richness or when membership vectors collapse to singleton roles.

layer2.mapping: Maps player performance data to latent role profiles via probabilistic soft assignment; GSI infers role structures using Bayesian posterior sampling.
layer2.telemetry: Interpretability score of role profiles and archetype recovery rate.

primitives.name: Archetypal Unit Identification
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Inference via **MCMC in NIMBLE**; label switching handled post hoc by probabilistic relabeling (`label.switching`); identifiability anchored by **archetypal units** (players with max membership ≈ 1).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'πik': 'membership weight of player i in profile k (dimensionless)', 'Archetype_k': 'set of players with dominant membership in profile k (players)'}
primitives.assumptions: Players with dominant membership (~1) define role archetypes; label switching occurs but is corrected.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When no player has strong dominance (>0.9) in any profile.

layer2.mapping: Derives interpretable role prototypes from posterior samples; GSE uses these as basis for player state transition modeling.
layer2.telemetry: Number of archetypal players identified per profile and label stability across runs.

primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S': 'number of posterior samples (dimensionless)', 'θs': 'posterior sample of parameters (dimensionless)', 'p(xi | θs)': 'likelihood of observation xi under parameter θs (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Marginal likelihood approximates true model evidence; singular models allowed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When WAICm fails to distinguish between competing model classes.

layer2.mapping: Selects best number of roles (K) based on out-of-sample predictive accuracy; GSI uses this to validate role taxonomy.
layer2.telemetry: Correct-K selection rate in simulations and cross-validation performance.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core idea of partial membership models is that football players do not belong exclusively to one role but rather exist in a probabilistic mixture of roles. This is modeled using a Dirichlet prior over membership vectors πi ∈ Δ^K, where Δ^K is the K-simplex. Each player’s observed count data xij is assumed to follow a Poisson distribution whose rate is a product of profile-specific rates λkj raised to the power of the corresponding membership weight πik. The generative process thus encodes role ambiguity as a multiplicative composition of latent profiles and soft assignments. The model is estimated via Bayesian inference using MCMC in NIMBLE, with label switching resolved post hoc. Archetypal units—players with maximal membership in a single role—are used to anchor identifiability. Model selection proceeds via marginalized WAIC (WAICm), which evaluates model complexity and predictive accuracy. These primitives enable GSI to extract interpretable role structures from multivariate performance data, while GSE leverages them for dynamic player state transitions and role-based forecasting.
